requirements: Concern actions must use an explicit policy matrix covering allowed actors, confirmation strength, rationale requirements, lineage effects, reversibility, and audit fields.
Concern lifecycle transitions must be compensating-action based (reopen/reverse lineage/successor records), not history erasure.
Help content must preserve canonical term names across Expert and ELI5 modes; only explanatory depth changes.
Orchestrator widget hostability must narrow to Progress while Seams/Node Graph/Evidence/History/Ledger remain native surfaces.
Widget semantic scope must inherit page/router context (project, focused run, live vs historical) and avoid independent run/lane scope drift.
Cross-surface routing must prefer receipt/attempt/usage identity over tier-era or run-only pivots, with explicit trust-state gating for stale/degraded projections.
Runtime/provider identity contracts must include requested/effective account context and actor scope beyond run-only records.
Project summary state must distinguish activity, attention, and health with blocked-owner routing and trust disclosure.
decisions: Concern dismiss/accepted-risk/lineage edits default to strong confirmation with required rationale; acknowledge/reopen may use lighter confirmation.
Adopt three-depth help contract: inline help, context help, canonical help entries.
Use app-default plus project override for Orchestrator Progress widget layout persistence.
Treat quiet/suppression as notification behavior, not concern dismissal.
Use blocked-episode and command-catalog canonical payloads as the basis for recovery and mutation routing across surfaces.
data_shapes: Canonical actor envelope: `project_id`, `actor_kind`, sparse actor refs (`run_id?`, `attempt_id?`, `thread_id?`, `wizard_id?`, `interview_id?`) plus requested/effective runtime-account identity.
Trust disclosure payload across surfaces: freshness/trust state, last update metadata, degraded reason, and mutation gate reason.
Usage bridge requires one authoritative `usage_event_ref` locator shape reused by receipts, artifacts, Usage, Ledger, and deep links.
routing_rules: Concern structural actions (`merge/split/supersede`) require guided lineage flows rather than one-click toggles.
Palette/shortcut/context actions must share the same confirmation and gating policy; discoverability cannot weaken safety.
Historical-mode views must remain anchored to focused historical run/attempt context; widgets cannot silently follow live scope.
Project badges/cards/title-bar/attention surfaces should share one status vocabulary and precedence (blocked over attention_required over advisory).
verification_rules: Canonical concern history must not be hard-deleted in normal operations.
`dismissed` and `resolved` semantics must remain distinct; `resolve` should carry explicit `resolution_kind`.
Schema consumers must not rely on tier-era identifiers or forbidden canonical names where newer contracts have replaced them.
Stale/degraded projection visibility is not mutation authority; runtime revalidation is required before sensitive actions.
owner_consumer_obligations: Orchestrator, Run Graph, Usage, Widget, and GitHub surfaces must converge on shared command payloads and trust-state behavior.
GitHub integration must bind reconnect/recovery to canonical project+actor context and effective account identity while preserving auth realm separation.
Project summaries should expose a dominant blocked/attention owner and reason to route users to the correct next surface.
stale_retirement_items: Retire concern-action behavior that mirrors lightweight toast/widget dismissal semantics.
Retire widgetized assumptions for non-Progress Orchestrator tabs.
Retire login-keyed durable GitHub identity in favor of stable internal account identity.
Retire tier-boundary/tier-era routing semantics where canonical package/seam/lane/attempt contracts now apply.
